$comment: SPEC §7.4 mock presets. Every SDK embeds this data byte-for-byte equivalent and expands it with the rules below. src/mock-presets.ts is the reference implementation; scenarios.json pins the expanded results.
rules: Let T be the first target of the configured target set in canonical order (PROTOCOL §1). In every template, replace the exact string "{provider}" with T.provider and "{target}" with T's string form (e.g. github:octocat), including inside longer strings such as ids.
The result is { signedIn, disabled: false, mock: true, targets: <canonical target strings>, supporter, contributions, fetchedAt: null, stale: false, fromCache: false } with no `unavailable` key.
supporter is the expanded `supporter` template when signedIn is true, otherwise null. contributions are the expanded preset contributions, in order.
Custom mock data ({ contributions: [...] }) yields signedIn: true, the expanded supporter template and exactly the given contributions (not rewritten).
Mock mode performs no network and no disk access. State changes below live in memory, per SDK instance.
signIn() resolves immediately; afterwards the instance is signed in. If it was signed out (preset signed-out, or after signOut), its contributions become [].
signOut() resolves immediately; afterwards getFinancialContribution() returns the signed-out shape (signedIn: false, supporter: null, contributions: []) with mock: true.

openCheckout(opts) resolves immediately with { status: "contributed", contribution } where contribution is the expanded `checkout` template with: provider and target from opts.provider when it names a configured provider (else T); amount = { value: opts.amount ?? 500, currency: opts.currency ?? "USD" }; frequency = opts.frequency ?? "monthly"; kind = "one_time" when frequency is one_time else "recurring"; status = "paid" when frequency is one_time else "active". The instance becomes signed in and the contribution is appended to its contributions (replacing an existing one with the same id).

Precedence: SPONSORKIT_DISABLE=1 beats mock (result is the disabled shape with mock: false). The `mock` constructor option beats the SPONSORKIT_MOCK environment variable. An unknown preset name throws SponsorkitError{code: "invalid_config"}.
